categories.main_business_segments: Lattice Semiconductor operates as a single business segment focused on the design, development, and sale of low power, small form factor Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) and related solutions. The company serves three primary end markets: Communications and Computing, Industrial and Automotive, and Consumer. It also generates revenue from intellectual property (IP) licensing, patent monetization, and design services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Lattice's core technology is its proprietary FPGA platforms, including the Lattice Nexus (28nm FD-SOI), Nexus 2, and Avant (16nm FinFET) platforms, which emphasize low power consumption, small size, and high performance. The company operates a fabless model, outsourcing wafer fabrication to leading foundries such as TSMC, Samsung, UMC, and Epson, and assembly/testing to OSATs like ASE and Amkor. Lattice also invests in advanced packaging, design software (Lattice Radiant, Propel), and integrated solution stacks for applications like edge AI, embedded vision, and hardware security.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Lattice's primary customers are OEMs in the Communications and Computing (servers, data centers, 5G infrastructure), Industrial and Automotive (factory automation, robotics, ADAS), and Consumer (smart home, wearables, AR/VR) markets. The company sells mainly through global and regional distributors, with Arrow, Weikeng, and Macnica being major partners, and also serves customers directly. Distributors accounted for 89% of revenue in 2024, with a significant concentration in Asia.
categories.geographic_coverage: Lattice operates globally, with the majority of its revenue (65% in 2024) coming from Asia, followed by the Americas (20%) and Europe (15%). The company has R&D and operational facilities in the US, Canada, China, Philippines, India, and Malaysia, and maintains sales offices in major metropolitan areas worldwide. Its products are shipped to customers in over 20 countries.
categories.supply_chain_position: Lattice is a fabless semiconductor company, positioned downstream in the supply chain. It designs and markets FPGAs and related solutions, relying on third-party foundries for wafer fabrication and OSATs for assembly and testing. The company focuses on product and market development, leveraging external partners for manufacturing and logistics.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Lattice's strategic focus is on delivering differentiated, low power programmable logic solutions for high-growth applications such as edge AI, 5G infrastructure, platform security, and factory automation. The company emphasizes rapid innovation, platform-based product development, and investment in proprietary software tools and solution stacks. R&D is centered on new FPGA architectures, advanced packaging, software development, and application-specific hardware/software solutions, with a global engineering presence.
categories.revenue_model: Lattice generates revenue primarily through the sale of silicon-based FPGA products and related hardware, with additional income from IP licensing (including HDMI/MHL royalties), patent sales, and design services. The majority of sales are made through distributors, with revenue recognized upon shipment or delivery of IP/services. Licensing and services revenue is variable and can fluctuate based on the timing of large transactions.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Lattice competes with larger FPGA vendors (such as Xilinx/AMD and Intel/Altera), as well as ASIC, ASSP, and microcontroller providers. The company differentiates itself as the leader in low power, small form factor FPGAs, targeting applications where power efficiency, size, and rapid time-to-market are critical. Lattice is considered a niche player with strong positions in edge and mid-range FPGAs, often winning designs where its unique attributes are valued.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2024, Lattice reported $509 million in revenue, down 31% from $737 million in 2023, reflecting cyclical softness in industrial, automotive, and telecom markets. The company maintains strong gross margins (66.8% in 2024) and a solid cash position ($136 million at year-end 2024). While recent growth was negative due to industry headwinds, Lattice has a track record of profitability and expects future growth from AI-related and edge applications.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Lattice emphasizes industry-leading low power consumption, small form factor, and ease of use as its core differentiators. Its FPGAs enable faster time-to-market, flexible design, and integration of advanced features (such as AI, security, and connectivity) in compact, energy-efficient packages. The company positions itself as the go-to provider for programmable logic in applications where power, size, and rapid innovation are paramount.
